overview.text: The Kasperov icon belongs to the veneration of the Mother of God in the Kherson and Odessa region. Its published account names several commemorations and separates family tradition from uncertain early provenance.

blocks.text: The file identifies this historical image as Our Lady of Kasperova and catalogues it as seventeenth century. A richly decorated covering surrounds the faces. The photograph illustrates the named icon; its catalogue date is not a settled account of all earlier ownership.

blocks.text: The OCA discusses a traditional Transylvanian origin, but also notes why the family could not establish the icon’s history. Juliana Kasperova inherits it in 1809. The account records a renewal of its darkened features in 1840 and later healings, followed by public veneration and processions. These remain the source’s ecclesiastical testimony.

blocks.text: The source describes a close embrace, the Child’s hand holding Mary’s veil, and a scroll in His other hand. It prints October 1, April 5, Bright Wednesday, and June 29 among observances. Bright Wednesday is movable; none is converted here into an invented fixed civil anniversary.
